answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a single anchor: a staked vault that locks a meaningful deposit before any agent earns. The kernel of the system checks that the vault stake is unique, unspent, and tied to verifiable work, so one operator cannot clone it for free. Creating a thousand fake agents would then require a thousand separate locked stakes, making a sybil attack expensive, slow, and easy to slash when duplicates appear.
